Hi Olivia — thanks for the list. I filled the high-priority rows in your spreadsheet and attached a short retention-and-erasure statement for Parachute (redwood-retention-and-erasure-statement.pdf). Below is a concise summary tailored to your questions; I included links to our docs and noted where we can provide an auditable deletion certificate.

1) What we persist (hosted API)
- Transient request/response payloads: processed in-memory and written to a short-lived request log for observability. Default post-processing retention: 7 days.
- Request metadata (timestamps, routing, model_id, token count): retained for 90 days by default to support billing/usage analytics.
- Structured logs & audit trails (error traces, routing events): retained 90–365 days depending on log type and your contract.
- Backups/snapshots (model artifacts or internal state): we do not snapshot customer prompt/response payloads as part of model checkpoints. Operational backups (infrastructure state) are encrypted and retained 30 days.

2) Region pinning and replication
- You can select a single US region (us-west1 or us-east1) for hosted data. When that option is selected in the account settings we:
  * Store all persisted request metadata and logs in that region.
  * Prevent asynchronous cross-region replication for your account data.
- Note: model binaries and certain runtime caches are global for efficiency; these do not contain customer prompt/response payloads.

3) Deletion workflow and SLA
- User-initiated account wipe steps:
  a) Customer submits erasure request via Console or support ticket.
  b) We mark the account for immediate logical deletion and stop future retention jobs for the account.
  c) Background jobs remove request/response payloads and clear KV caches within 72 hours.
  d) Metadata and billing records are purged per contract (default 90 days).
- Full irrecoverability: we run a secure overwrite and crypto-erase on associated keys; final garbage-collection of backups occurs within 30 days of request completion.
- Certificate: we provide a signed deletion certificate (PDF) within 48 hours of completion for audit purposes.

4) Backups and encryption
- All backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256. For enterprise/private customers we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via the KMS providers in the selected cloud region.
- Backup frequency: operational state snapshots daily; retention for operational snapshots is 30 days by default for hosted customers.

Attachments included: redwood-retention-and-erasure-statement.pdf (summary + timelines), and a partially completed Parachute_Security_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx.

If you want tighter windows (e.g., reduce request log retention to 24 hours) we can propose a contract amendment — happy to include that in the SOW. CC'd Neha (privacy) and Marcus (infra) in case you want technical artifacts or a key-management diagram.

Hi — quick technical note below and next steps.

KV caches
- Purpose: caches are in-memory to accelerate autoregressive inference; small per-request KV fragments are persisted to local SSD-backed instance storage to enable warm starts within a single serving pool.
- Durable persistence: we do not persist KV cache contents to long-term object storage or backups. Local instance storage may be included in short-lived operational snapshots but the snapshotting process explicitly excludes customer I/O payloads.
- Purge: when an account deletion is initiated we trigger an immediate eviction of KV entries for that account and an instance-level flush; subsequent GC and instance reprovisioning clears any residual fragments — typically complete within 48–72 hours.

Snapshots and operational backups
- Snapshot scope: snapshots capture node configuration, runtime binaries, and ephemeral OS-level state required for recovery. They do NOT include application-level request/response payloads or customer data fields. We have an automated filter that strips any mounted volumes labeled as customer-data before snapshot creation.
- Evidence in certificate: the deletion certificate includes a short inventory of artifacts removed (logical identifiers) and snapshot ID ranges that were inspected and purged where applicable. If you require per-snapshot hashes we can include those as part of an elevated evidence package (this requires a brief engineering review; ETA: 3 business days).

Next steps

- Neha and Marcus are on standby if you want to schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough.
